text:
Anna Li: Heads-up — support ticket #8472 (cust: Acme) reporting p99 chat latency spikes since ~03:40 UTC. p95 looks OK but p99 jumped from ~420ms -> 1.8s. They send lots of short prompts with similar prefixes.
Samir Patel: Thanks Anna. Any KV/cache miss metrics or recent rollout?
Anna Li: Rolling telemetry: kv_prefix_miss_rate for their org_id jumped 2% -> 26% at 03:41. No infra deploys in that window. Autoscaler stable.
Mike Chen: I'm seeing correlated logs from the runtime: many keys with high cardinality like `acct:acme:user:<session>` getting churned. Eviction churn on LRU node. Paste of aggregated log snippet:
```
[03:40:59] kv_lookup key=acct:acme:user:bf2c miss=true eviction_policy=LRU evicted=acct:acme:user:7a1d
[03:41:00] kv_warmup start prefix=acct:acme weight=8
[03:41:01] kv_lookup key=acct:acme:bot:resp miss=true
[03:41:02] kv_stats prefix_miss_rate=0.26 hotset_entropy=0.85
```
Anna Li: Ticket includes cURL repro hitting our hosted API in bursts (10 req/s bursts for a few org users). They use same prompt template causing long tail of distinct prefix keys.
Samir Patel: Ok probably prefix-key cardinality + uncoordinated warmup causing cache thrash. Two tracks: short-term mitigations and long-term fixes. Short term: 1) throttle burst ingestion via per-org smoothing token-bucket 2) temporary increase shard cache_size for the org 3) enable prefix normalization to collapse session-level suffixes.
Jessica Torres: For short-term we can do a canaried config override for their org id. I can push override to increase kv_shard_size by +20% and bump ttl to 60s for 2h. Will that be enough?
Mike Chen: It should reduce eviction pressure quickly. Also recommend turning on the new warmup-stagger window (alpha) to avoid simultaneous warmups on many prefixes. Command to run admin prewarm (for emergency):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.dev/_admin/prewarm \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"org_id":"acme","prefix":"acct:acme"}'
```
Samir Patel: We should also add a temporary circuit-breaker: if prefix_miss_rate > 15% for org -> route to slower fallback model with higher cache affinity (less prefix diversity). That avoids p99 blowouts while we stabilize.
Anna Li: Support has asked for repro steps to show it's cache thrash. Mike, can you paste the specific query pattern we should run?
Mike Chen: Repro script (simulates many short sessions):
```python
# simulate bursty short sessions to reproduce p99
import requests,random,uuid
for t in range(500):
  key = f"acct:acme:user:{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
  payload = {"prompt": "{{user}} says hi".replace("{{user}}", key)}
  requests.post("https://api.redwood.dev/v1/chat", json=payload, headers={"x-org-id":"acme"})
```
This gets miss rate up in ~60s in our staging cluster.
Jessica Torres: After short-term stabilization we'll schedule rollout of two long-term fixes: 1) prefix-key normalization library (strip session suffixes by default for known templates) 2) implement LFU-based eviction for prefix namespaces with high churn.
Samir Patel: Add also a telemetry alert: prefix_entropy > 0.7 & p99 > 1s -> auto-mitigation job triggers. Ticketing: ENG-8472, SRE oncall notified.
sre-bot: Pager alert created: ENG-8472 p99-latency spike, assigned to @Samir Patel and @Jessica Torres :rotating_light:
Anna Li: I'll coordinate with support and ask Acme for a short maintenance window to run the prewarm + config override. If they can't, we'll apply server-side override and monitor.
Mike Chen: I'll run the repro in staging and attach flame graphs. Early note: hotset_entropy climbs fast when session suffix length > 6.
Jessica Torres: Plan for next steps: 1) apply canary override now (Jessica) 2) run staging repro and capture metrics (Mike) 3) if stable, roll to prod for Acme only (+ rollback plan) 4) schedule eviction policy change for next sprint.
Samir Patel: Sounds good. I'll draft postmortem template and add a follow-up for per-prefix SLA guidance.
Anna Li: Thanks team. Marking thread for follow-up in 2 hours with metrics. :thumbsup:
